subject: Discovery recap: migration off proprietary LLM APIs -> open models
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Samuel Jones <samuel.jones@brightcommerce.com>, Priya Menon <priya.menon@brightcommerce.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap: migration off proprietary LLM APIs -> open models

Hi Samuel / Priya —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery call and next steps so we have a shared reference. I captured the pain, current stack, success criteria, and an initial model compatibility shortlist. Please let me know if I missed anything.

Pain points you shared:
- Rising cost of OpenAI + Anthropic usage (esp. completions and embeddings) across heavy-search and generation workloads.
- Vendor lock-in concerns: reliance on proprietary APIs for function-calls/streaming causes fragility in experimentation.
- Latency spikes and unpredictable tail latency impacting user experience for interactive product features.
- Data residency and audit requirements for certain EU customers.

Current stack / usage notes (as discussed):
- Core infra: product backend on GCP, orchestrated with Kubernetes; web + mobile UX.
- API usage: OpenAI for chat/completions; Anthropic used for safety-sensitive reranking/assistant in a few flows.
- Typical request profile: 50-100 RPS at peak for embeddings/search, bursty generation workloads for content personalization.
- ML infra: limited on-prem GPU capacity for internal experiments; all production inference is hosted with vendor APIs today.

Success criteria for migration/P0 metrics:
- Cost: target 3x reduction in per-unit inference cost for high-volume embedding/generation paths.
- Latency: p95 < 250ms for short-turn chat/generation (where feasible).
- Compatibility: parity for function-calling, streaming, and structured output to avoid major product refactors.
- Security/compliance: ability to host in VPC regions + KMS integration; SOC 2 evidence.
- Quality: automated evals show no more than 5% degradation on key prompts compared to current models.

Initial model shortlist we discussed (for POC):
- Llama 3 family (instruction-tuned variants) - good ecosystem support and quantization options.
- Mistral 7B/Mix instruction variants - competitive inference cost, strong instruction performance.
- Falcon-40B-Instruct (quantized) - good for higher-quality generation when needed.
- RedPajama / MPT derivatives - exploratory for embedding parity.

Compatibility requirements:
- API parity for streaming and function/tool calling (or a shim layer to emulate behaviors).
- Support for KV cache reuse and prefix-caching to preserve session performance.
- Quantized model variants (4-bit/8-bit) preferred to hit cost targets.

Next steps (agreed on call):
1) We (Redwood) will deliver: a short discovery PDF + proposed POC plan (attached).
2) BrightCommerce to complete the security questionnaire (attached) and share a data-flow diagram for the production path.
3) Schedule a technical deep-dive with your engineering team (30-45m) - propose Tue/Wed next week.
4) Draft SOW / POC success criteria for review (we can iterate after the tech deep-dive).

Attachments: discovery-recap-BrightCommerce.pdf (this summary), BrightCommerce_security_questionnaire.xlsx (blank copy we asked you to fill), sample SOW template.

If that aligns, I’ll get the POC plan and proposed tech deep-dive times over to you this afternoon.

Best,
Marissa
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
From: Samuel Jones <samuel.jones@brightcommerce.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 15:37:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: migration off proprietary LLM APIs -> open models

Thanks Marissa - this is great and captures everything we talked about. A couple of clarifications:

- On cost: the 3x target is correct for our long-term goal; for the POC we'd be happy with 1.5-2x to show directionality.
- On latency: the <250ms p95 is for chat snippets only; longer generation paths (batch content gen) can tolerate higher latency.
- On compliance: we need the KMS + VPC hosting for EU customer data specifically; US traffic can stay in vendor-hosted regions for now.

We’ll fill out the security questionnaire and share the data-flow diagram by EOD Monday.

Also looping in Priya (product lead) - Priya, we should prioritize the tech deep-dive so we can validate function-calling parity.

Best,
Sam
Director of Product | BrightCommerce

Perfect - thanks Sam. Two quick notes:

- For the POC we’ll scope one high-volume path (embeddings for search) + one interactive path (chat with function calls). That will let us validate cost, latency, and compatibility in parallel.
- Aditya will own the technical deep-dive; I’ll share proposed times for Tue/Wed 06/22-06/23. Aditya - can you take a look at availability and any pre-reads you want from BrightCommerce?

Marissa
